1.1.1.title: 1.1.1 Non-text Content (A)
1.1.1.html:
Benefits

Success Criterion (SC) 1.1.1 Non-text Content ensures accessibility for users with visual or hearing disabilities by providing text alternatives for meaningful images, icons, charts, graphs, and audio-only content (like podcasts). It also prevents decorative content from cluttering screen reader output.

WCAG Requirements

All non-text content (visual and audio) must have a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose, OR must be ignored if purely decorative. Specific examples include:

  • Images used as links or controls (e.g., icon buttons): Active images need a descriptive text alternative or accessible name that serves the same purpose and meaningfully conveys the image's function.
  • Informative images: Images (and icons) that convey content must have a descriptive text alternative that serves the same purpose and presents the same information as the image.
  • Complex images: Images that are too complex to be fully described in a short text alternative must have their purpose described using an extended text alternative, such as descriptive text paragraphs or an accessible data table.
  • Decorative images: Images that are decorative or have content already conveyed in text must not be given a text alternative that is exposed to assistive technology.
  • Audio or Video (time-based media): Text alternatives must be provided to identify the purpose of the video or audio content.
  • CAPTCHA: Interactions designed to verify human users must not rely on a single sense.

Salesforce Accessibility Standards

None at this time.

Best Practices

None at this time.

Testing Protocol

  1. Identify any non-text content on the page. This may include icons, graphs and charts, photographs, illustrations, decorative images, or video/audio content.
  2. Ensure all non-text content that is meaningful has an appropriate text alternative conveying its purpose, OR is ignored by assistive technologies if solely decorative. Techniques include:
    • Use a screen reader and navigate to the image or icon. Listen for a text alternative in the speech output, or if decorative, listen to make sure it is skipped over.
    • If the image is a graph or chart, ensure there is a long-form text alternative such as a paragraph or a table somewhere in the page content.
    • Right-click the element and inspect it using the inspect tool.

Example Bugs

  • An informative image <img> is not given an alt attribute, which causes screen readers to read only the image's filename.
  • A decorative image without informational content is not ignored with a null alt attribute alt=""
  • An image with an alt attribute of alt="Empty Alt" - screen readers will read "Empty Alt" rather than ignoring the image.
  • There is no long-form text equivalent presented that presents the data within a chart or graph.

Not a Bug

  • If an image repeats information already presented in text, it does not necessarily need alternative text and can be ignored by assistive technology with a null alt attribute: alt=""

Techniques and Bug Fix Recommendations

  • Informative images <img> must have an alt attribute conveying the information in the image, such as alt="Codey giving a thumbs up"
  • SVG images must have proper text alternatives (e.g., with role="img" and an alt attribute, or an aria-label conveying the information).
  • Icons must have a label describing the function of the icon. For example, aria-label="Search" instead of aria-label="Magnifying Glass"
  • Purely decorative and non-informative images <img> must be ignored by assistive technology by giving them a null alt attribute: alt=""
  • Purely decorative and non-informative SVGs must be ignored with aria-hidden="true" or role="none".
  • Complex images such as charts must be conveyed in text, e.g., with descriptive paragraphs or a data table with equivalent information.
  • Time-based media (video or audio-only content) must at minimum be given a text description of its purpose.

Bug Priority and Impact Levels

  • P1 (Accessibility: Task blocking): Alt text descriptions are not provided for informative images, OR interactive elements like navigation items and buttons use images without providing text alternatives.
  • P2 (Accessibility: Difficult to use): Complex images exist and are exposed to screen readers, but long-form description is missing.
  • P3 (Accessibility: Limited impact): Decorative images contain duplicative alternative text, leading to redundant announcements, OR decorative elements are missing alt="" or aria-hidden="true".

Resources

  • Success criterion: 1.1.1 Non-text Content
  • Deque University (requires login): WCAG 2.2 Conformance Testing Methodology SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content
1.1.1.remediation:
• Informative images must have an alt attribute describing the content
• SVG images must have role="img" and aria-label or alt attribute
• Icons must have labels describing their function (e.g., "Search" not "Magnifying Glass")
• Decorative images must use alt="" or aria-hidden="true"
• Complex images (charts/graphs) need descriptive text or data tables
• Time-based media needs text descriptions of purpose

1.2.1.title: 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A)
1.2.1.html:
Benefits

Success Criterion (SC) 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) benefits users who have visual or hearing disabilities. The purpose of this SC is to make sure that any prerecorded time-based media that contains only audio or only video has an alternative that presents equivalent information.

WCAG Requirements

  • Prerecorded audio-only media: An alternative for time-based audio must be provided. It must present equivalent information to the prerecorded audio-only content.
  • Prerecorded video-only media: An alternative for time-based video (without audio) must be provided, OR an audio track is provided that presents equivalent information to the prerecorded video-only content.

Exception: When audio-only or video-only content is both of the following, it is exempt from this SC:

  • The audio or video is an accessible media alternative for text
  • The media is clearly labeled as such

Salesforce Accessibility Standards

None at this time.

Best Practices

Place a transcript or a link to the transcript immediately following or adjacent to the media player to ensure it is easy to find.

Testing Protocol

Audio-only media:

  1. Identify any prerecorded audio-only media on the page, such as a podcast.
  2. Ensure there is a text-based alternative (generally a transcript) for each audio-only media file.
  3. Verify that the text alternative/transcript:
    • Is accessible to all users (e.g., can be accessed with screen readers)
    • Includes essential dialogue (not paraphrasing)
    • Identifies the speakers
    • Describes essential sound effects

Video-only media:

  1. Identify any video-only media (e.g., silent demo).
  2. If the video is decorative or repeats information available in text, a text or audio description is not required.
  3. For informative visual content in the video-only file such as text on the screen, important scene changes, or character expressions, check that one of the following is true:
    • A transcript or other text description provides equivalent information to what is presented visually.
    • A synchronized soundtrack provides equivalent information to what is presented visually.

Example Bugs

  • A podcast is provided without a text-based alternative such as a transcript.
  • A silent product demo is provided with no audio track and no equivalent transcript/text description to describe what is happening.

Not a Bug

  • If a video is only decorative, such as an animation provided for ambience with no informative content, it is exempt from this SC.

Techniques and Bug Fix Recommendations

  • A transcript is generally the simplest way to make sure audio-only or video-only content is accessible for everyone.
  • For decorative animations and videos, ensure they are ignored by assistive technology by adding an empty alt="" (for images) or aria-hidden="true" (for video files).

Bug Priority and Impact Levels

  • P1 (Accessibility: Task blocker): Prerecorded audio-only files do not come with a descriptive text transcript, OR prerecorded video-only files (no dialogue) do not come with a text or audio description of what happens on the visual track.

Resources

  • Success criterion: 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
  • Deque University (requires login): WCAG 2.2 Conformance Testing Methodology SC 1.2.1 Audio or Video-only (Prerecorded)
1.2.1.remediation:
A transcript is generally the simplest way to make sure audio-only or video-only content is accessible for everyone.

For decorative animations and videos, ensure they are ignored by assistive technology by adding an empty alt="" (for images) or aria-hidden="true" (for video files).

1.2.2.title: 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A)
1.2.2.html:
Benefits

Success Criterion (SC) 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) primarily benefits users with hearing disabilities when watching prerecorded videos with audio content. Users who cannot hear will benefit from captions that are synchronized with the audio content.

This SC deals with prerecorded video. For live video, see 1.2.4 Captions (Live).

WCAG Requirements

Synchronized captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media (media with audio synchronized to the video).

Captions must provide an experience that is equivalent to that of the audio track. This means:

  • Captions must be synchronized with the audio content.
  • Speakers must be identified in the captions if it is not obvious who is speaking.
  • Important/meaningful music and sound effects must be identified when necessary to understand the content.

Exception: When synchronized media content is both of the following, it is exempt:

  • The content is a media alternative for text
  • The content is clearly labeled as such

Salesforce Accessibility Standards

None at this time.

Best Practices

None at this time.

Testing Protocol

  1. Identify any prerecorded video with audio.
  2. Determine whether there is a way to enable captions.
  3. Verify that the captions provide an equivalent experience to the audio by making sure:
    • Captions are synchronized with the audio content.
    • Speakers are identified in the captions.
    • Important/meaningful music and sound effects are identified when necessary to understand the content.

Example Bugs

  • A prerecorded video is available without synchronized captions that match the audio.

Not a Bug

  • The captions need to be synchronized with the audio content and in the same viewport, but don't necessarily have to be overlaid at the bottom of the video. For example, if there is a scrolling transcript in a panel directly to the right/left of the video that is also synchronized with the audio, this is sufficient since the user can consume both video and captions at the same time.

Techniques and Bug Fix Recommendations

  • Ensure there are synchronized captions available in the same viewport as the video for all media with video and audio.

Bug Priority and Impact Levels

  • P1 (Accessibility: Task blocking): Prerecorded multimedia files (video with audio files) lack or contain inadequate text-based synchronized captions.

Resources

  • W3C: Captions/Subtitles
  • Success criterion: 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded)
  • Deque University (requires login): WCAG 2.2 Conformance Testing Methodology SC 1.2.2 - Captions (Prerecorded)
1.2.2.remediation: Ensure there are synchronized captions available in the same viewport as the video for all media with video and audio.
